sources.title: Explanatory Note - Draft Planning Agreement, Penrith City Council and Microsoft Datacenters (Australia) Pty Limited
sources.publisher: Penrith City Council and Microsoft (prepared jointly)
sources.notes: Published with the draft agreement for notification (9 March to 6 April 2023). States the $8,423,505.96 monetary contribution, payable before the first construction certificate, for land, embellishment and public works, calculated by the Mamre Road East Precinct s7.11 rates because no contributions plan applied to the land. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/councils/penrith/ (sha256 bad583725e35, 203,336 bytes); PDF not committed, text is.

sources.title: Planning Agreement, Penrith City Council and Microsoft (draft notified 2023, file dated 3 February 2022)
sources.notes: Clause 6.1: $8,423,505.96 or that amount indexed by CPI, whichever is greater. The council publishes the executed agreement (signed 7 June 2023) beside it, but the executed copy is a scan with no text, so whether its figure is the same has not been read. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 (sha256 0cc10e1ebad4, 4,132,478 bytes); the executed copy too (sha256 9ffd9e9ac258, 1,639,832 bytes), its text empty.

sources.title: Voluntary Planning Agreement - Microsoft Datacenter (Your Say Penrith)
sources.notes: Voluntary Planning Agreement between Penrith City Council and Microsoft Datacenter (Australia) Pty Ltd for Lot 2 DP 1271142, 769 Mamre Road, Kemps Creek, within the approved industrial estate 'The Yards' at 657-769 Mamre Road. Publicly notified 9 March to 6 April 2023; endorsed by Council at its Ordinary Meeting of 29 May 2023; executed 7 June 2023. Purpose: to collect monetary contributions for the future development of a data centre, to support delivery of infrastructure including open space and landscaping embellishment within the Mamre Road Precinct. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/councils/penrith/ with the three documents it links (SRC_PENRITH_VPA_NOTE, SRC_PENRITH_VPA_DRAFT; the executed copy is a scan).

sources.title: Estimating Data Centre 'Phantom Demand' (research briefing, 21 November 2025)
sources.notes: Subtitled 'Surging data centre connection requests drive phantom demand for power'. Finds 6 in every 7 MW of the 44 GW of connection requests AEMO received are 'phantom demand'. The page says AEMO separately commissioned Oxford Economics to forecast data centre electricity use, and that 'This research briefing was commissioned by AWS.' Cited by the BCA (Submission No 116, under its subtitle), Data Centres Australia and the NSW Data Centre Guidelines. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/oxfordeconomics/.

sources.title: Business Council of Australia - Membership (Our Members)
sources.notes: The BCA's own member directory, served in full to the research crawler on 2026-10-22 (it returned a challenge page in September): 130 members, each with its web address. Its data-centre-related members: AirTrunk, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Blackstone, Goodman, Stockland, TransGrid, Endeavour Energy, Fujitsu, Telstra, Origin Energy and Tata Consultancy Services. Not listed: NEXTDC, CDC, Equinix, Macquarie Technology Group or Data Centres Australia. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/bca/ with the about page.

sources.title: Investment Delivery Authority to turbocharge business investment in NSW (ministerial media release, 23 June 2025)
sources.publisher: NSW Government - the Premier, Treasurer, Minister for Innovation, Science and Technology, Minister for Planning and Public Spaces
sources.notes: $17.7 million in the 2025-26 Budget to establish and support the Investment Delivery Authority; about 30 large projects a year; projects over $1 billion; a multi-agency Investment Taskforce in Investment NSW under the Premier's Department. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/nswgov/.

sources.title: Quarterly report on foreign investment - 1 January to 31 March 2026
sources.notes: 311 commercial proposals approved in the quarter, 97 of them with conditions. Reports by sector and source country only; 'Any data that may enable the identification of a particular person or organisation has been suppressed'. Does not mention data centres. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 (sha256 10906032a6df, 941,813 bytes); PDF not committed.

sources.title: 2026 ministers' diary disclosures (NSW Cabinet Office index page)
sources.notes: Lists each minister's quarterly diary disclosure for 2026. The disclosures themselves sit under /sites/default/files/noindex/, which nsw.gov.au's robots.txt closes to crawlers; the 30 for the Premier, Treasurer and the Planning, Energy and Industry ministers from January 2025 to June 2026 were not fetched (data/raw/registers/nsw_ministers_diaries/refused.json; docs/requests/DOWNLOADS.md). The index pages for 2025 and 2026 ARCHIVED 2026-10-22.

sources.title: NSW Data Centre Guidelines
sources.notes: Six principles, 17 numbered performance measures. Primary source for dPUE/dWUE limits, Group 6 diesel limits, 25% demand-flexibility requirement, PPA additionality criteria. Footnote 4 cites 'Oxford Economics, Estimating Data Centre Phantom Demand, Oxford Economics, 2025', introduced as the work of the firm 'which prepared AEMO's forecast'; that briefing's own page says it was commissioned by AWS (SRC_OXEC_PHANTOM_2025). ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/nswgov/ with a SHA-256 manifest (an earlier copy is at data/raw/nsw_planning/).

insert.notes: The same report's forecast for 2025 to 2030, of which $1.1bn is described as excess capacity for public use. CLAIMED: operator-supplied data and a forecast.

set.notes: Claimed by Data Centres Australia to the NSW inquiry on 1 May 2026: operators will pay $10.3 billion in energy infrastructure to 2030. TRACED 2026-10-22 (RG-043): the report behind the industry's figures (Mandala, commissioned for Data Centres Australia by AirTrunk, AWS, CDC and NEXTDC) gives $3.1bn invested 2020-2025 and $7.2bn forecast 2025-2030, which together make $10.3bn; the only '$10.3 billion' the report itself states is the Australian Government's grid funding to 2030. Its figures come from 'data from select data centre operators'.

Data Centres Australia: of the $10.3 billion, $1.1 billion is excess capacity available for public use. TRACED 2026-10-22 (RG-043): in the Mandala report the $1.1bn is the excess within the $7.2bn forecast for 2025-2030; it puts the excess built 2020-2025 at $0.5bn. Neither figure has been tested against network capital plans.

The NSW Data Centre Guidelines: 'Oxford Economics, which prepared AEMO's forecast on data centres, estimates 6 in every 7 megawatts (MW) of data centre connection requests are phantom demand', citing Oxford Economics' briefing 'Estimating Data Centre Phantom Demand' (2025). CORRECTED 2026-10-22 (RG-078): that briefing's own page says it 'was commissioned by AWS'; AEMO's forecast was a separate engagement.

add_sources.quote: 6 in every 7 MWs of connection requests are estimated to be ‘phantom demand’. | This research briefing was commissioned by AWS. The analysis and findings are Oxford Economics.

set.notes: Oxford Economics, as cited in BCA Submission No 116: AEMO received around 44 GW of connection requests linked to data centre proposals in 2025. CORRECTED 2026-10-22 (RG-078): earlier notes called this research 'for the BCA'; the briefing's own page says it 'was commissioned by AWS'.

set.notes: ADVANCED 2026-10-22 (research batch 3). Traced to source: Data Centres Australia told the inquiry operators 'will pay $10.3 billion in energy infrastructure to 2030, and $1.1 billion of that is excess capacity'. The report behind the industry's figures (Mandala, commissioned for Data Centres Australia by AirTrunk, AWS, CDC and NEXTDC) gives $3.1bn invested 2020-2025 and $7.2bn forecast to 2030, built from 'data from select data centre operators'; the two make $10.3bn, and the only '$10.3 billion' the report states is the Australian Government's grid funding. Its $1.1bn excess is within the forecast, with $0.5bn before. The networks told the inquiry the principle holds - Ausgrid: 'the customer who caused network costs pays for them'; Transgrid invests only on 'full commitment' and had no data centre commitment on 22 May 2026 - but none put a total on it. Still to test: the quantum against Transgrid, Ausgrid and Endeavour capital plans and AER determinations (aer.gov.au did not answer).

we don't invest in new equipment, new assets, long lead items or anything ... until we have that full commitment.
